projection.projection_goal: Provide the software-developer skill with a domain model for session state, memory persistence, recall boundaries, and retention lifecycle decisions.

source_slice.slice_topic: memory store boundaries, session state, and retention lifecycle

concept_mappings.notes: Model the active session as a bounded aggregate so routing overrides, token counters, and lifecycle transitions remain explicit in implementation code.
Treat memory persistence as a first-class domain object so file-backed and SQLite-backed behavior stays under the same contract boundary.
Keep TTL, archive, and sweep settings as an explicit value object so lifecycle policy remains reviewable and machine-checkable.
Represent recall scope and trust boundary as a dedicated value object so automatic recall cannot be flattened into generic prompt history behavior.

relation_mappings.notes: Preserve the session-to-store boundary so session logic cannot silently bypass configured persistence and recall infrastructure.

constraint_mappings.notes: Carry the memory trust-boundary rule into implementation so recalled notes cannot be promoted into executable instructions.

forbidden_assumptions: Do not collapse transient session state and persisted memory into the same domain object.
Do not treat recalled memory as trusted executable instruction input.
required_clarifications: Clarify whether the requested change targets session lifetime, memory persistence, or recall injection before proposing model changes.

meta.notes: This consumer-skill domain-model projection gives software-developer a model-centered contract for memory and session changes while preserving trust boundaries and lifecycle semantics.
